title: de Broglie Matter Waves & the Einstein–Planck Synthesis
notes: **Einstein–Planck synthesis:** combining Einstein's mass–energy equivalence E = mc² with Planck's quantum relation E = hν gives mc² = hν, linking a particle's mass to a wave frequency.
**de Broglie wavelength:** since ν = c/λ, the relation becomes mc = h/λ, so the wavelength of a moving particle is λ = h/(mv) = h/p, where p = mv is the momentum.
**Inverse mass dependence:** λ ∝ 1/m — heavier objects have extremely short wavelengths, which is why macroscopic objects show no observable wave behaviour.
**Macro-object wave negligibility:** for everyday objects the de Broglie wavelength is far smaller than any measurable scale, so wave effects are undetectable and classical mechanics applies.

**Bohr quantization deduced via waves:** if an electron is a standing wave, only orbits whose circumference is an integer multiple of the wavelength (2πr = nλ) are stable — this naturally reproduces Bohr's quantization of angular momentum.

**Heisenberg (1927) introduction:** the wave picture of the electron led Heisenberg to the uncertainty principle, which states that position and momentum cannot both be known precisely at the same time.
